findings.evidence: R1 says to deliver recognition and corrective feedback separately, 'never in the same conversation or message.'
findings.fix: Keep separation as the default to avoid a feedback sandwich, but allow a context-sensitive combined conversation when the user explicitly needs one and the recognition is genuine and clearly distinct.

findings.evidence: For all corrective feedback and expectation resets, the skill says to 'send a written recap within one working day.'
findings.fix: Make the timing a default subject to the user's agreement, workplace policy, confidentiality needs and the importance of the conversation; preserve the recap template.

findings.evidence: The lateness branch permits recording a health or family reason 'unless they ask for it to be written down', while the SKILL.md confidentiality test excludes health and family details and requires policy and need-to-know checks.
findings.fix: Align the branch with the confidentiality test: leave personal details out of ordinary recaps and notes even on request, and direct any necessary accommodation documentation to the appropriate authorized process.

findings.evidence: The dispute test says an assertion is an inference if the other person cannot dispute it 'by pointing to a record'. An observed interruption may have no record, while a recorded accusation can still be an inference.
findings.fix: Distinguish firsthand observable behavior from interpretation, and separately check the available evidence and acknowledge uncertainty; do not require a record for every observation.
